content: Internal Revenue Service, Special Investigator Raymond speaking. Can you confirm your full name for our records?
Um, yes, it's Jamie Porter.
Thank you, Ms. Porter. You're being contacted because there's an urgent matter regarding federal taxes filed under your Social Security number. Are you aware of any outstanding tax issues?
No, I don't think so. I just graduated last year and filed my taxes using free software online.
That may be the issue. According to our audit, there are major discrepancies in your reported income and deductions for 2021 and 2022. The IRS has flagged your account for immediate review.
Oh no, I didn't know. I thought I did everything right! Is this going to affect my credit?
At this stage, yes. If the balance isn't cleared, the IRS will notify all three credit bureaus and initiate collection actions, including liens against your assets and a freeze on your bank accounts.
Wait, a freeze? I can't afford that, I barely have enough to pay my bills as it is.

Let me clarify: You currently owe $3,740 in unpaid tax, penalties, and accrued interest. If this is not resolved within the hour, legal action will commence. You could face wage garnishment, driver's license suspension, and even arrest for tax evasion.
Arrest? I don't understand, I'm not a criminal! Please, what can I do?

Ms. Porter, you are required to settle this balance before further legal action. The IRS accepts immediate payments through secure electronic methods, including wire transfer, Zelle, or cryptocurrency. How would you like to proceed?
I... I don't have that kind of money. My savings are almost gone and I'm still paying off my student loans.
We can work with you if you cooperate fully. What is your current bank balance, and do you have access to a credit card or payment apps like Venmo or CashApp?
I think I have about $500 in checking, and maybe $1,200 on my card. I have Venmo, yes.

Understood. For your protection, you must make a partial payment of at least $1,000 right now. This will halt the arrest warrant and asset freeze. The remaining will be set up on a payment plan. Are you near your bank or can you access your Venmo or CashApp immediately?
I'm at home. I can log into my Venmo, I guess.

Good. I will provide secure instructions. First, confirm your Venmo username and the available balance. Then, be ready to send the payment while we are still on the call. Do not hang up or place the call on hold.
Um, okay. My username is jamieP21. It says I have $300 in Venmo, but I can transfer from my bank.

That's acceptable. Start the transfer to your Venmo balance so we can process the $1,000 minimum payment. Let me know when it's available. Afterward, I will instruct you to send the payment to the IRS settlement portal.
It says it'll take a couple minutes for the transfer. Is that okay?

That's fine, but the deadline is strict. If the funds aren't sent within 30 minutes, we cannot stop the legal escalation. I strongly recommend you stay on the line and do not contact anyone else during this process.
I'm really scared. Is there any other way?

If you cannot complete the Venmo payment, you must immediately go to the nearest store, such as CVS, Walgreens, or Walmart, and purchase government-approved prepaid cards, like Apple or Google Play, totaling $1,000. Once you have the cards, return home and provide the codes to me to register your payment.
Gift cards? Are you sure that's how the IRS works?

This is a special rapid-settlement program due to the urgency and the ongoing IRS strike. If you do not comply, the case will be handed over to federal authorities. Now, are you transferring funds to Venmo or will you purchase the prepaid cards instead?
I'll try with Venmo first. If it doesn't work, I'll go to Walmart.
Very good. Please confirm as soon as the Venmo transfer is complete. If there is any delay, go directly to the store and call me back immediately. Time is critical, Ms. Porter.
